questions.answer: A fair amount, yes. I take care of my own room and help out at the weekend. I can't say I enjoy it, but there's a certain satisfaction in a [[tidy]], well-organised space.

questions.q: Which household chore do you dislike the most?
questions.answer: Washing dishes, without a doubt. After a big family meal there's always a mountain of them, and it seems to take forever. I'd much rather sweep the floor or do the shopping than face that [[seemingly endless]] pile.

questions.q: Did you help with housework as a child?
questions.answer: A little. My mother expected us to make our beds and keep our school things in order. At the time I [[grumbled]] about it, but looking back, those small responsibilities taught me to look after my own space.

questions.q: Is housework shared equally between men and women in your country?
questions.answer: Not yet, honestly. Traditionally, women have done most of it, and that's still common. However, younger couples, especially in cities, are increasingly sharing chores, which I see as a [[welcome shift]].

questions.q: Do you think children should do housework?
questions.answer: Yes, within reason. Simple chores like tidying their room or setting the table teach responsibility. It also stops them from [[taking for granted]] how much work goes into running a home.
